name: Reverse Crunch on Incline Bench
description: The reverse crunch performed on an incline bench elevates the head end above the hip end, adding gravitational load to the lower abdominal region throughout the movement compared to the flat-bench version. The athlete grasps the bench behind the head, extends the legs below horizontal, and pulls the knees toward the chest by posteriorly tilting the pelvis — a movement almost exclusively controlled by the lower rectus abdominis. The incline increases both the eccentric and concentric challenge.

execution.starting_position: Lie on the incline bench with the head at the high end. Grasp the bench behind the head. Legs are extended, lowered below the hip level.
execution.setup_instructions: Set the bench to 20–30° incline. Ensure the head-end grips are within comfortable reach.
steps: Step 1: Begin with legs extended and lowered below the bench plane (against the gravity).
Step 2: Curl the pelvis backward (posterior tilt) and draw the knees toward the chest simultaneously.
Step 3: At the top, the knees should be at or above the hip level and the lower back is lifted off the bench.
Step 4: Slowly lower the legs back down, resisting the eccentric pull.
Step 5: Return to full extension without letting the legs drop rapidly.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale as the knees come toward the chest. Inhale on the controlled descent.
common_mistakes: Using momentum from the legs rather than initiating with posterior pelvic tilt
Not lifting the lower back off the bench at the top — full contraction requires this
safety_considerations: If grip fatigue limits reps before the core does, use wrist straps
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Legs from full extension below horizontal to knees drawn to chest with lower back lifted.
execution.tempo_recommendations: 2-1-3-0. Slow eccentric is essential on the incline version.
coaching_cues: Pull with the abs, not the hip flexors
Curl the tailbone up — do not just swing the legs
